//: Reviewed npm-audit exceptions: pnpm workspace (pnpm-lock.yaml).
An entry here suppresses ONE advisory id on ONE package name in the CI
dependency audit (scripts/security/check-npm-audit.sh, HIGH+CRITICAL gate).
The bar for adding one is high. The advisory must have NO fixed release to
upgrade to. The advisory must also not be exploitable in production, by
one of two bars. Either the package is absent from the production
dependency closure of every shipped workspace package
(`pnpm -r why <pkg> --prod`) and from every built artifact, with that
evidence in the PR; or present in a production closure only where
the vulnerable function is provably never called at runtime, with a
negative runtime test and a positive control, both recorded in the entry
(in its `reason`). A public tracking issue must exist so the entry is
removed the moment a fixed release ships. An advisory with an available fix
must be fixed by upgrading (or a pnpm override), never listed here.
Enforced by check-npm-audit.sh on every run: exact id + package match only;
every entry is printed; an entry past `expires` fails the run even after
the advisory disappears; `expires` may be at most 30 days out, so renewing
an entry means re-reviewing it; a malformed or missing file fails the run.
Entry format:
id       OSV/GHSA id exactly as osv-scanner reports it
package  npm package name exactly as osv-scanner reports it
reason   which bar applies and the evidence for it (for the second bar, the negative runtime test and positive control), and the tracking issue as #<number>
expires  YYYY-MM-DD (UTC), the last day the exception is honoured

exceptions.reason: Applies to the zod@3.25.76 copy only; every 4.x copy in the lockfile resolves to 4.6.7 (patched, >= 4.6.6). No fixed release in the 3.x major as of 2026-10-23 (advisory range is every version below 4.6.6; first patched is 4.6.6, a different major). The copy is pinned exactly (zod 3.25.76) by @expo/cli@57.0.27, and moving it to 4.x would break the Expo CLI, which uses the zod 3 API. `pnpm -r why zod@3.25.76` shows @expo/cli as its only lockfile parent, reached only via breeze-mobile → expo (Expo CLI, declared as an expo runtime dependency); no other workspace package resolves it. The advisory is memory exhaustion from validating an attacker-supplied oversized array, and the Expo CLI only validates local app config on dev/EAS build hosts. breeze-mobile neither declares nor imports zod. Not shipped in any server image: the api, web, portal and m365 executor Docker deps stages do not install breeze-mobile. NOT verified for this entry: the Hermes bundle source-map check used for the node-forge and braces entries has not been run for zod; run it before renewal. Remove this entry when a newer @expo/cli drops or upgrades the pin. Tracking: #9915

No fixed release as of 2026-11-18: the advisory covers <= 4.0.7, 4.0.7 is the latest published version, and it lists no patched release (upstream fix PRs micromatch/picomatch #257-#270 are open, none released). Covers the 4.0.4 and 4.0.7 copies. Second bar: present in a production closure, but its vulnerable path (lib/parse.js, compiling an attacker-supplied pattern such as +(*a)) is never called at runtime. `pnpm -r why picomatch --prod` at main e697b5fc2c reaches only @breeze/web, @breeze/portal and @breeze/docs (astro -> @astrojs/internal-helpers) and breeze-mobile (expo -> @expo/cli, Metro). web and portal: `astro build` bundles picomatch 4.0.7 into dist/server/entry.mjs, and its only caller there is @astrojs/react's component filter, built only when the react() integration sets include/exclude. Both bundles bake include: undefined and exclude: undefined, so the filter is null. Astro's memory cache provider (query.exclude globs) is not configured or bundled. The other picomatch users (vite-plugin-assets, content glob loader) run only at build time. Negative runtime test: copies of both built servers, with counters on picomatch(), its posix wrapper and lib/parse.js parse(). Booted and sent requests whose path, query keys, query values and headers carry +(*a) payloads: 0 picomatch and 0 parse calls (web: 40 @astrojs/react check() calls, portal: 3, so islands did render), every response under 600 ms. Positive control: the same instrumentation with include: ['**/*.+(tsx|jsx)'] records 1 picomatch and 1 parse call in each server. The pattern is still build-time config even then, never request input. Shipped copy vulnerable: picomatch 4.0.7 '+(*a)' against 'a'*n+'b' takes 0.9/3.4/14.4/56.7 ms at n=18/20/22/24 (x4 per 2 chars); a config-style pattern takes under 0.05 ms. docs is a static build: 0 of its dist files contain picomatch (control: the same grep finds it in the web server bundle). mobile: `expo export` source maps of the Android (2,733 modules) and iOS (2,735 modules) Hermes bundles at expo 57.0.33 have 0 picomatch, micromatch, anymatch or metro-file-map sources; controls expo-secure-store and react are present. No client bundle of web or portal contains it. Not reachable from the api image. Tracking: #12155
